m:opera: The roof is free and always open, 24 hours a day, no ticket (travel guides). Inside, the foyer is free; performances and guided tours are paid (times on operaen.no, not read). The marble floor can be slippery in rain or ice: from November, take care.
m:munch: Open Monday, Tuesday and Sunday 10am–6pm, Wednesday to Saturday 10am–9pm (museum website). Adult ticket 280 kroner (about €26) by day and 200 kroner (about €18.60) in the evening after 6pm, according to a 2026 guide: to be confirmed on munch.no. Closed on 1 May; reduced hours on 24 and 31 December. «The Scream» and other versions are shown in rotation between MUNCH and the Nasjonalmuseet: check the museum website for what's on display on the days of your visit.
m:akershus: The main gates are open from 6am to 9pm every day; from October to April the side gates too, from 7am to 9pm (official website of the area). Entry to the fortress and the Armed Forces Museum is free; other exhibitions, the Resistance Museum (about 80–100 kroner, about €7.50–9.50) and guided tours are paid. It's a military area and can close at short notice: if you find a gate closed, go through the Visitor Centre (+47 23 09 39 17).
m:radhuset: Open Monday to Saturday from 9am to 4pm, closed on Sundays; free entry with a security check at the entrance (Oslo City Council website). The website lists some closing days between October and December 2026 and warns that more may be added: check oslo.kommune.no the day before. Some rooms may be closed for events. Free guided tours run «sometimes»: I couldn't find the times.
m:slottet: The park around the palace (Slottsparken) is open to all year-round. The changing of the guard in front of the palace is every day at 1:30pm (travel guides, to be confirmed). Tours of the palace interiors aren't always scheduled and normally run only in summer: check royalcourt.no.
m:vigeland: The park is open 24 hours a day, free (travel guides). The nearby Vigeland Museum is paid separately (price and hours not read). Daylight is short in autumn and winter: in mid-October the sun sets around 5:30pm, in December around 3:15pm, so it's best to go in the middle of the day.
m:nasjonal: Adult ticket about 220 kroner (about €20.50; sources vary from 160 to 220, under-18s free): to be confirmed on nasjonalmuseet.no. Hours vary between the sources I read: the most complete gives 10am–5pm Tuesday to Sunday, closed on Mondays (open on Mondays too in June–August); another mentions evening openings. Closed on 24, 25 and 26 December, 31 December and 1 January. Check the hours on the website.
m:brygge: The promenade is always free. The Nobel Peace Center, in the old Vestbanen station, costs about 180 kroner (about €16.80, a mid-2026 guide: another gives 130): from September to mid-June it's open Tuesday to Sunday 11am–5pm (Wednesday until 8pm) and closed on Mondays (guide, to be confirmed on nobelpeacecenter.org). The restaurants on the waterfront are expensive: for a coffee or a quick lunch, better to move on.
m:fram: From October to April open every day from 10am to 5pm; adult ticket 180 kroner (about €16.80) according to a 2026 guide (other sources give 170): to be confirmed on frammuseum.no. The combined Fram and Kon-Tiki ticket costs 325 kroner (about €30). The summer ferry from Rådhusbrygga doesn't run in winter: take bus 30. The Viking Ship Museum on Bygdøy has been closed since 2023 for works and should reopen in 2027 (date not yet confirmed): for Viking finds there's the Museum of Cultural History in the centre (about 140 kroner).
m:holm: From October to December open every day from 10am to 4pm (24 and 31 December 10am–2pm); adult ticket 200 kroner (about €18.60, museum and tower included), under-30s 150 kroner (official website). The ski jump tower is closed from 13 to 16 October for maintenance: on those days the museum and the view from the square are still a good visit. Take metro line 1 to Holmenkollen stop.
m:grun: The riverside walk is always free. Mathallen is open Tuesday to Friday 10am–8pm, Saturday 10am–6pm, Sunday 11am–5pm, closed on Mondays (guide, to be confirmed): some stalls close earlier, especially on Sundays. On Mondays Grünerløkka is still a good walk but some cafés are closed.
vd:tim: The café of one of the world's most famous roasters, in Grünerløkka: a small counter where you drink an espresso or a filter of single-origin coffee, carefully made.
vp:tim: An espresso costs about 48 kroner, a filter 55 and a latte 52–60 (about €4.50–5.60, prices from a 2026 guide, not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:supreme: A roastery and café on Grünerløkka's main street, with espresso and filter coffee from beans roasted on site: a simple place for breakfast or a break between stops.
vp:supreme: An espresso costs about 45–55 kroner, a latte about 58 (about €4.20–5.40, prices from a 2026 guide, not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:mathallen: Oslo's food hall, in a former factory by the river: about thirty stalls with fish soup, Norwegian open sandwiches (smørbrød), cheeses, cured meats, Asian dishes and pastries. Pick a stall and eat at the shared tables.
vp:mathallen: Lunch usually costs 115–180 kroner (about €11–17): fish soup with bread about 120–150, smørbrød 75–130. Hours from a 2026 guide, not seen on the website; on Sundays some stalls close earlier. Closed on Mondays.
vd:godt: A cooperative bakery in Grünerløkka, known for its sourdough bread and kanelboller, cinnamon buns: a simple, good Norwegian breakfast, with coffee.
vp:godt: A kanelbolle costs about 40–50 kroner, a loaf or a pastry 55–90 (about €3.70–8.40, guides, not seen). Hours: only the weekday opening (7am) appears in guides; closing time and weekends are a cautious estimate, to be checked.
vd:sara: An informal café-restaurant in Grünerløkka with soups, salads, open sandwiches and a good beer list: a simple lunch or a no-frills dinner, in a neighbourhood setting.
vp:sara: Lunch costs about 120–180 kroner, evening dishes 180–250 (about €11–23, guides, not seen). Hours not found: I've put a cautious range, check before going.
vd:elias: A seasonal kitchen with many vegetarian dishes, in Grünerløkka: lunch has a soup of the day and fresh dishes at mid-range prices.
vp:elias: Lunch costs about 145–185 kroner (about €13.50–17, guides, not seen). Hours not found: I've put a cautious range, check before going.
vd:olympen: An old 1892 tavern-beer hall in the Grønland area, with high ceilings and chandeliers: home-style Norwegian dishes like kjøttkaker (meatballs in gravy), lapskaus (stew with vegetables) and, in autumn, fårikål (lamb with cabbage).
vp:olympen: A main course costs about 200–295 kroner (about €19–27.50, guides, not seen). Hours not found: I've put a cautious range, check before going.
vd:engebret: A historic 1857 restaurant near the fortress and the City Hall, frequented by artists: traditional Norwegian cooking with fish, meat and autumn seasonal dishes such as fårikål.
vp:engebret: Fårikål as a main course costs about 265–295 kroner (about €25–27.50, guides, not seen): it's a mid-priced place. Hours not found: I've put a cautious range, check before going.
vd:egget: A breakfast and lunch bistro in Majorstuen: eggs on toast and open sandwiches in a quiet setting, near the Frogner district and Vigeland Park.
vp:egget: Eggs on toast and smørbrød cost about 85–150 kroner (about €8–14, guides, not seen). Hours not found: I've put a cautious range, check before going.
vd:solberg: A café of a historic Oslo coffee roaster on the Aker Brygge waterfront: a cheaper break than the harbour-front restaurants, with a coffee or a pastry.
vp:solberg: A coffee costs about 45–60 kroner (about €4.20–5.60, estimate from guides, not seen). Hours not found: I've put a cautious range, check before going.
cd:kontiki: Thor Heyerdahl's raft, on which he crossed the Pacific.
cd:folkemuseum: A hundred historic buildings in the open air, including a stave church.
cd:astrup: Contemporary art in a Renzo Piano building.
cd:nobel: Where the Nobel Peace Prize is celebrated, with an exhibition on the laureates.
cd:fiordo: Two hours among the islands, in front of the city.
cd:maritimo: The story of fishermen and Vikings, on the Bygdøy peninsula.
